findings.element: .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick — the single accent-filled mark on the horizontal measure; broken by [data-app="timeline"][data-medium="sheet"|"full"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: -28px } at _gate-suite.html:7785-7786 outranking [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) } at :8297
findings.problem: Direction B's whole claim is that position on the measure is daysFromToday x pixels-per-day computed from real dates. In the ACROSS layout the one mark the design accents as "this one, next" is the only mark plotted at the wrong distance. Measured at 1920x1000 (?layout=across): .b-item for 'Menu tasting at The Orchard / Sat 1 Aug / 16' anchors at x=524.5, and its title, its date, its '16' and its own stem (.b-item::after, left:0) are all at 524.5 — but its .b-tick centre is at 496.5, exactly 28px left. Every other tick sits dead on its anchor (dx=0.0 at days 23, 37, 44, 51, 65, 79). The dot is visibly detached from the stem that points at it. The specificity is the cause: the desk-medium lead override is (0,5,0) and beats the across-axis rule at (0,4,0), so `left: 0` never reaches the lead mark while it correctly reaches all six others. 28px is not a constant error in days — the rail is 1602px/79d at 1920, so it reads 1.4 days early; 1.97 days early at 1440, 2.30 at 1280, and 4.73 days early at 768 (rail 468px/79d), where the mark for Sat 1 August lands where Monday 27 July belongs. Identical on ink and on paper. The DOWN axis is correct (all ticks dx=-23.5), so it only misreads on the axis whose entire job is horizontal distance, and both gates pass because neither compares a tick's centre to its item's anchor.
findings.fix: Add one rule after _gate-suite.html:8300 so the across axis governs the lead mark as it already governs the other six: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; }` — (0,5,0) and later in the file, so it beats :7786. Cleaner if you would rather not stack a counter-rule: scope both desk overrides to the vertical axis by inserting `.b-measure:not([data-across="true"])` after the [data-medium] compound at :7781-7782 and :7785-7786, leaving the down axis byte-identical. Then add the assertion the gates are missing: for every .b-item on the across measure, |tick centre x - item anchor x| <= 0.5px.

findings.element: header.tlHead > span.word ("timeline") — [data-app="timeline"] .tlHead { padding: 40px 40px 0 }, vs .head { height: 60px; padding: 0 28px } for tasks and .head { padding: 10px 30px } for notes
findings.problem: The suite's argument is that nothing rebuilds when you cross the rail, and the wordmark on the sheet's head is the object that proves it. It does not hold still. Driven through .rail [data-rail=...] at 1920x1000 and re-measured on every crossing (stable, repeatable): span.word box top is y=37.0 for tasks and y=38.1 for notes — the two agree within 1.1px — and y=58.0 for timeline. Timeline's word also sits on a 25.5px leading against 22px/21.76px for the other two, so its baseline lands 22.8px lower, and the box bottom moves 59.0 / 59.9 / 83.5. Same font, same 17px, same weight 600: nothing but padding puts it there. Clicking Timeline and clicking back drops and lifts the identity by a visible amount, which is the one motion the architecture promises will not happen. It also spends a 66px band on a single 70px word and then builds a second head (div.b-bar, 56px, carrying the project name and the three acts) 40px below it, where tasks and notes carry identity, project, facts and actions on one 60-62px line. (The horizontal difference — 128 / 471 / 140 — is defensible: each wordmark aligns to its own product's measure. The vertical is not aligned to anything.)
findings.fix: Land the timeline wordmark on the line the other two already share: `[data-app="timeline"] .tlHead { height: 60px; padding: 19px 40px 0; }` and `[data-app="timeline"] .tlHead .word { line-height: 22px; }`. That puts the box top at y=37 and the leading at 22px — pixel-identical to tasks and within 1.1px of notes — and lifts the stage 6px. Verify by asserting it: span.word's bounding top must be equal within 1.5px across the three data-rail crossings at 1920, 1440 and 1280.

findings.element: section.tray[data-lane="waiting"] > .trayHead > .trayNote, sized by [data-app="tasks"] .board:has(> .tray[data-lane="waiting"][data-empty]) { --col-waiting: var(--rail) } at _gate-suite.html:1789 (--rail: minmax(132px,172px))
findings.problem: The empty lane yielding its width is a decision, stated in the comment at :1782. The prose staying full-width inside the yielded track is not. Measured at 1920x1000: To do / In progress / Review / Done are 372px each, their .trayNote sits on one 17px line, .trayHead is 50px, and all four first cards start at y=197. Waiting is pinned to 172px, so 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.' wraps to two lines (34px), its .trayHead is 67px, and its only content starts at y=227 — 30px below the four cards beside it. Constant at 1680, 1440 and 1280 (172px every time). In the 1100-1199 band, where the 258px lane floor at :3412 has not engaged yet, it compounds: at 1100 Waiting is 139px with a THREE-line note (head 83px, content at y=344), Review wraps to two (head 67px, first card y=314) and the other three stay at 50px/298 — three head heights and three first-row baselines in one five-lane row, spanning 46px. The row of five lane heads is the strongest horizontal line on the board, and it is the one line that does not hold.
findings.fix: Stop the yielded lane carrying body prose in its head. Add beside the five --col rules at :1786-1790: `[data-app="tasks"] .board:not([data-filtered]):not([data-blank]) > .tray[data-empty] .trayNote { display: none; }`, and move the sentence into the empty body so nothing is lost — render .trayEmpty as "Nothing held up. This lane holds anything waiting on a reply, a delivery or a decision." (it is the lane's only content and can wrap freely). All five .trayHead boxes then measure 50px and all five first rows start on one baseline at every width. Separately, extend the designed floor over the band above it: change `@media (max-width: 1099px)` at :3412 to `@media (max-width: 1199px)`, so 1100-1199 gets the same 258px scroller as the band below instead of 203px lanes whose second head also wraps.
